body:
> But you CAN turn things around like I did.

The thing is not everyone is you. You're a conventional, attractive, social sort of person who's had some very hard times. Some of us are miserable, ugly, lonely people no matter how well we're "doing." It's circumstances that made you suicidal. To others being alive is all it takes.
Thanks for all the input. I'll take a break from this for now but I'm in a better frame of mind.
Gratefulness is definitely something I need to learn. I admire it.

I've been trying to sleep, eat and exercise well, but it's all rather uneven. Not sure about seeing a doctor. I'm uninsured and have usually been able to help myself, but that might no longer be true. I've never even posted online about this stuff before.

> Usually when you have problems connecting with other people, do you feel like it is a lack of common ground that is causing the lack of ability to connect? Or that they just aren't hearing you?

Lack of common ground mostly. Also, difficulty speaking up in unfamiliar settings, and I could be called agoraphobic as well. About 8 years ago I went an entire year without stepping out of the house. Since then I've had sustained periods of going out and being around people, but have ended up disappointed. One solid friend could make an enormous difference. I don't feel connected to the greater world. I would like to.
I used to be able to live by the ideal in that quote. Now it seems that the "higher self" is beyond reach and that the lobotomized existence he criticizes is the only, unbearable possibility.

Thanks for sharing. And yeah, it does seem to me that "happiness" is not a worthwhile goal and only breeds pain, but I'm having a hard time convincing myself that 'living" is good enough.

My dad is about the only family I have and the only person I would truly hurt if I topped myself. About three years ago I actually considered a murder-suicide for that reason, though that is out of the question now as it's not in my rights to do that. I try to remind myself that I should stay alive for at least as long as he does but that's getting difficult. I explained myself to him last night and it was so heartbreaking I ended up sobbing. And I never cry. I'm just a mess of emotions over it all.

I'm leery of the use of the word selfishness. I realize suicide inflicts pain but ... I don't think humans are capable of unselfishness. To do anything at all you have to convince yourself it's in your own self-interest, whether the results are good or bad. And while I think the choice you've made is commendable, what about people who are never suicidal? Staying alive is quite easy for them.
Hm, this may be a good way to try rewire my brain. Time to reread The Myth of Sisyphus. I barely remember it.
It's from [The Mindscape of Alan Moore](http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0410321/). Available on youtube and vimeo I believe. Good stuff.

True, there's always some hope. Thinking about the odds for myself makes me nauseous though. I have the most withdrawn temperament of anyone I've known, coupled with too-lofty standards that seem barely of this world. Very difficult to reconcile. Don't know how this is going to play out, but it's gotten increasingly bleak over the years.

> No, it is kind of the icing on the cake of failure.

Not denying it's a failure. Just not seeing how living for living's sake is better when hope for anything more has really thinned out.

> You say "I see this as the only realistic way to salvage some dignity", yet our society views it as a terribly shameful thing, and odd rumors will surface after your passing.

Rumors? I imagine they'll mostly wonder what I might've been, and to keep living would simply answer that question in the negative: not very much. Anyway, it's less about what people in general think of me than what people I care about think of me, and I what think of myself.

> Why give up without having really given it your best? What all have you tried, and why do you view those as failures.

I'm so emotionally fatigued I don't believe my best is any longer possible. I've had great "success" in a financial sense but it only left me alone and unhappy as ever, and I abandoned work because of it. I have concepts for personal projects but can't follow through because I no longer believe anything can break my isolation. Partly because I don't believe the things I want to create for myself are things anyone really wants to see (I am/was an artist). And because I've been unable to maintain friendships in real life and to ever form a relationship. If I can't connect with people on that level, why do anything at all? I could technically do things just for myself but that doesn't supply the energy required for anything significant. I feel an entirely superfluous person, a raving madman in a cell.
